title: What comes right before the verb

sections.content: The word carrying new or emphasized information sits right before the verb — Hungarian's 'focus position'. Ma otthon vagyok puts ma (today) in focus: 'It's TODAY that I'm home.' Move otthon there instead — Otthon vagyok ma — and the emphasis shifts to WHERE, not WHEN.

items.spanish: Ma otthon vagyok, most pedig tanulok.
items.english: Today I'm home, and right now I'm studying.

sections.content: There's no single 'neutral' word order in Hungarian the way English leans on subject-verb-object — whatever sits right before the verb is what the sentence is really about.
